title: Layer-based blemish removal, selective redness correction, and eye brightening (Day 23) in Photoshop
summary: This PHLEARN tutorial demonstrates non-destructive, layer-based retouching in Photoshop. The instructor walks through starting with blemish removal on a dedicated new layer using the Remove Tool (with Auto mode), then performing targeted color corrections by isolating redness with a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer and an Eyedropper, followed by precise masking to confine edits to skin areas while preserving lips. The workflow proceeds to brighten the eyes with a Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer, using inverted and carefully painted masks to isolate eye regions. The session ends with a quick organizational step—grouping layers—and a quick before/after comparison, plus a note about downloading a PSD to study the edits non-destructively.
topics: Changing brush color for visibility (chartreuse vs magenta)
Context for what to remove (spare features, e.g., mole) vs distractions
Applying removal on a separate layer for easy revision
Eyedropper tool to sample specific red regions
Cranking hue and saturation to visualize edits
Fine-tuning with Hue, Saturation, and Lightness sliders
Masking the hue/saturation effect with a layer mask
Using a brush to reveal/hide edits on the mask (white reveals, black hides)
X key to swap foreground/background for masking
Inverting layer masks (Ctrl/Cmd + I or contextual menu)
Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer for eye brighten
Downloading the PSD to study edits

sections.title: Intro, setup, and blemish removal on a new layer
sections.description: Intro to Day 23, goals for basic retouching, and the setup of a dedicated new layer for removing blemishes and distractions. The instructor highlights removing spots, redness, and minor distractions, with emphasis on getting consent from the subject for removal decisions and establishing an order for edits.

sections.title: Targeted color correction with Hue/Saturation (Red)
sections.description: Introduction of the Hue/Saturation adjustment layer. The Reds channel is targeted, the Eyedropper is used to select the precise red area (e.g., on the subject's nose). The instructor demonstrates how dialing hue, saturation, and lightness affects only the chosen red regions, and how to reset controls to fine-tune the effect.

sections.title: Masking to constrain color edits (lips preserved)
concepts: paint over lips to preserve natural lip color
sections.description: Demonstrates adding a layer mask to the Hue/Saturation adjustment and painting with black over the lips so the color edit does not affect them, preserving a natural lip appearance while the rest of the face benefits from targeted redness correction.

sections.title: Eye brighten via Brightness/Contrast with selective masking
sections.description: A multi-step enhancement to brighten the eyes. The Brightness/Contrast layer is applied, its mask inverted, and then the eyes area is revealed with a soft brush (low flow) to avoid harsh transitions. The instructor covers adjusting brightness and contrast and provides tips for managing the mask and re-editing as needed.

sections.title: Wrap-up, grouping, and further tips
sections.description: Final review of the edits, grouping related layers for organization, and a closing note about downloading the PSD to study the workflow. The segment reinforces the non-destructive approach and previews next advanced retouching topics.
